title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: 15-second video and lower pricing
text:
Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: 15-second video and lower pricing

# Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and cost-effective with longer clips

Nov 05, 2026

 Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash brings 15-second clips, stronger consistency, and faster, more cost-effective generation. 

Anish Nangia

Product Manager, Google DeepMind

 

- We are launching Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash with support for fifteen-second videos and improved reference adherence.
- You can now edit clips through multi-turn conversations, which allows for faster adjustments without starting over.
- We reduced the price by 30% to help you produce high-quality video content at a lower cost.
- This model is generally available on the Gemini API and Google Cloud for your production needs.

Today, we’re rolling out Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, and making it generally available across the Gemini API and Gemini for business. Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash introduces native 15-second video creation, multi-turn conversational editing capabilities, and enhanced reference following. We have dropped the price 30% from Gemini Omni 1.1 making it available at $0.07 per second for 720p video.

...

## Fast and cost-effective at scale

Beyond the lower price, the workflow keeps costs down: you can draft fast at 360p or 720p, fix a detail with a follow-up edit instead of re-generating the entire clip, and then upscale your best creations to 1080p or 4K.

## Longer clips up to 15 seconds

You can now generate and edit videos natively up to 15 seconds long, up from 10 seconds with Omni 1.1. You can also specify duration in one-second increments from 3 to 15 seconds, giving you room to tell complete stories, create product explainers, or produce full social ad spots in a single generation.

...

Businesses, startups, and creatives are already using Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash in their workflows. And for the first time, Gemini Omni is now generally available, backed by Google Cloud’s enterprise-grade infrastructure and security. Provisioned Throughput is available, and outputs carry an imperceptible SynthID watermark.

...

While development is ongoing to further improve things like fast sports action, rapid script changes and complex physics, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is ideal for businesses, developers, and creators producing videos at scale. You can get started with Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash today as it rolls out across Google’s products and developer platforms:

- For developers using the Gemini API: Prototype in Google AI Studio, explore interactive starter apps, and check out the developer documentation and pricing.
- For businesses: Try it in the Google Cloud console, and build enterprise solutions with the API.
- For everyone using Google apps: Direct scenes and multi-turn edits in Flow, generate 15-second clips at no additional cost in Google Vids with a Google account or Google Workspace subscription, create 15-second videos in the Gemini app (rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers), and scale video campaigns in Google Ads.

title: U.S. Postal Service Recommends Shipping Price Adjustments ...
text:
Nov. 12, 2026

# U.S. Postal Service Recommends Shipping Price Adjustments for 2027

- Postal Service filed notice with regulator to increase prices for USPS Ground Advantage; Priority Mail and Priority Mail Express; and Parcel Select and some competitive special services.

- No changes are made to the price of stamps: First-Class Mail remains one of the best mailing bargains in the world.

- Pricing actions are part of a balanced approach under the Postal Service’s ongoing modernization plan aimed at achieving financial sustainability.

WASHINGTON — The Postal Service filed notice today with the Postal Regulatory Commission (PRC) for domestic and international shipping services price and fee changes. The changes will take effect on January 17, 2027. The proposed adjustments were approved by the USPS Board of Governors this week. The adjustments would raise domestic shipping services prices 5.9 percent on average for Priority Mail service, Priority Mail Express, USPS Ground Advantage and Parcel Select. 

The Postal Service will also convert the 8 percent transportation-related price change implemented in April of this year to a permanent 8 percent fuel surcharge, plus an additional 3 percent given the recent further elevation of fuel prices for a total of 11 percent. The surcharge, which will not impact international products at this time, will be reevaluated in July 2027 based on fuel prices in the first half of 2027. 

The Postal Service will also adjust prices on some competitive special services and introduce new fees that better align with the industry. This includes adjusting prices on some competitive special services, including but not limited to address enhancement services, premium forwarding services, and several competitive ancillary services; competitive PO Box prices will not be changing in January. 

In addition to increasing domestic competitive rates, the Postal Service is also adjusting international mail and shipping rates as well as the country rate group structure and group assignments. The adjustments will raise prices by an average of 7.9 percent for Priority Mail Express International, Priority Mail International, First-Class Package International Service, and International Priority Airmail. 

The Postal Service is also introducing a new optional Outbound Proof of Delivery service for Priority Mail International and expanding USPS Delivered Duty Paid (DDP) service to include International Priority Airmail. This change in the DDP service will allow outbound customers to pay the duties while mailing or at a later time.

Although mailing services price increases are based on the consumer price index, shipping services prices are primarily adjusted according to market conditions. The USPS governors believe these new rates will keep the Postal Service competitive while providing the agency with much needed revenue as it continues to struggle with financial issues.

...

The PRC will review the changes before they are scheduled to take effect. The complete Postal Service price filing, with prices for all products, can be found on the PRC website under the Daily Listings section at prc.arkcase.com/portal/filings. The Competitive Products filing is Docket No. CP2027-1. The price tables are also available on the Postal Service’s Postal Explorer website at pe.usps.com/PriceChange/Index.

title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen AI model: Know features, price, and more | Tech News - Business Standard
text:
# Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen AI model: Know features, price, and more

## Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen focuses on faster coding, research and AI agent workflows, with a 1 million-token context window, new safety features, and availability across consumer and developer tools

...

5 min read Last Updated : Nov 13 2026 | 11:50 AM IST

#### Listen to This Article

Google has introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, an artificial intelligence (AI) model designed to handle everyday tasks such as coding, research, data analysis and writing. The model focuses on speed and efficiency, particularly for tasks involving multiple steps, reducing the need for users to provide repeated instructions.

Unlike Google's Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon models, which are built for complex reasoning and longer tasks, Hydrogen is designed for faster execution across a wider range of applications. According to Google, the model is aimed at both developers and consumers and is being rolled out across the Gemini app, Google Search, Google AI Studio, the Gemini API and its enterprise services.

...

This allows Hydrogen to work with large documents, code repositories and other information without having to process everything in smaller, separate sections.

...

### Gemini 4 Hydrogen: Pricing

For developers accessing the model through the Gemini API, Google has set the price at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

Input tokens refer to the information provided to the model, including prompts and uploaded content, while output tokens refer to the responses generated by it. Google says the pricing remains the same across the model's one-million token context window.

The model is being made available across different Google products, although access and subscription requirements vary depending on the service being used.

For consumers, the model is available through the model selection menu in the Gemini app. It is also being integrated into Google Search for users globally.

Developers can access Hydrogen through the Gemini API, Google AI Studio and Android Studio. Paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can also use the model through Google Antigravity.

title: Meta Prices Muse Ember API at $0.10 per Million Input Tokens | TokenPost
text:
# Meta Prices Muse Ember API at $0.10 per Million Input Tokens

Meta also lists output tokens at $0.50 per million and describes Ember as its smallest reasoning model.

By Simon Yoon

Published Nov 10, 2026, 1:54 PM EST

A clear acrylic bar passes between two brass metering bowls / TokenPost.ai

Meta has added Muse Ember to its Model API as a lower-priced reasoning model than Muse Spark 1.3.

Muse Ember costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens.

Input and generated output are billed separately, so the total depends on how many tokens Ember receives and returns.

Meta lists Muse Spark 1.3 at $1.25 per million input tokens and $4.25 per million output tokens. At the lower Ember band, Spark 1.3 costs 12.5 times more for input and 8.5 times more for output.

Meta describes Ember as its smallest reasoning model. The Muse lineup is designed for tool use and mixed inputs, including text, images and audio, extending beyond text generation.

The broader Muse family also includes Muse Wonder, which Meta introduced in October for coding and agent work. Wonder is available through the Model API, and TokenPost previously covered the Muse Wonder models for coding and agent work.

title: Pay for your users, not their activity: why Ably now prices on monthly active users
text:
Pay for your users, not their activity: why Ably now prices on monthly active users

# Pay for your users, not their activity: why Ably now prices on monthly active users

One number decides your Ably bill now: monthly active users. Add Chat, Spaces or AI Transport and the price stays the same.

Matthew O'Riordan CEO and co-founder of Ably.

Nov 5, 2026· 4 min read

Ably now prices on monthly active users (MAUs). One number, and one you already know: how many people used your app this month. Know that and you know what you'll pay, before you've written a line of code and however busy those users turn out to be.

If you're an existing customer and wondering what this means for you: nothing changes unless you want it to. Your pricing stays as it is. The rest of this post is why we've done it and how it works.

...

Infrastructure is usually priced on consumption: queries, compute, storage. That's because the provider can only see how much you use, not what that usage is worth to you. Software used directly by people is usually priced per user, because headcount is something customers can forecast and budget for.

Ably sits between the two. It's infrastructure underneath, powering experiences end users interact with directly. Until now, we priced it like infrastructure. From today, Ably prices by monthly active user. That makes your costs far easier to predict and budget for. What you pay now scales with the value you get, which is largely how many people you serve, at a price that holds up at any scale.

...

This is the part I'm most excited about. 

We've heard it many times: a team wanted to add typing indicators, presence, a live cursor, some small realtime touch that would've made the product better, and held back because of what it would add to the bill. That's the last thing we want. 

On MAU the price doesn't move with which products your users use or how much (within the fair usage that comes with every package.) Add Chat, LiveObjects, Spaces or push notifications and your bill stays where it was. Same for AI Transport: agents and servers aren't users, so you pay for the person who got the answer, not the tokens it took to deliver it. We want what you want: more of your users getting more from your product.

## If you're already an Ably customer

Nothing changes for your account. If you're on resource-based pricing you stay on your current package, limits and terms, and we've no plans to change that. The one thing to know: if you change your package online from here, the packages on offer are MAU packages. Want to move sooner? Do it from your dashboard whenever you like. Estimate from your user count, or set a clientId on your end-user connections and your dashboard will show your actual MAU within a month. If you have a managed contract, talk to your customer success manager.

## How we count

An MAU is a person who actually used your app through Ably this month, identified by the clientId you set when they connect (one line in the SDKs), counted once however often they return. Servers and agents don't count. And because we count people who connect rather than people who have an account, if realtime powers one screen in a much larger product you pay for the people who open that screen, not your whole user base. The detail is in the pricing FAQ.

...

Start free. The Free package covers 500 monthly active users, which gets you further than you'd think, so build something and see your real numbers before you pick a package. Self-serve prices are published up to 50,000 users, and we've priced them to be competitive with any comparable platform.

# Google releases speed-focused Gemini 4 Hydrogen, with API pricing of $1.50 input and $7.50 output; also coming to the free Gemini app and Search

2026-11-13 04:05 (GMT+9)

Google on Nov. 12 (Nov. 13 Japan time) released its AI model "Gemini 4 Hydrogen." It is a new Gemini 4 model following the higher-end "Gemini 4 Carbon" and "Gemini 4 Argon," and Google positions it for handling everyday tasks, coding and AI agent work quickly and efficiently. According to Google, it finishes tasks 2.5 times faster than the current "Gemini 3.8 Flash." Developer API pricing is $1.50 for input and $7.50 for output per million tokens. It is rolling out from the same day to developers, businesses and general users, including free users of the Gemini app and all users of Google Search.

...

Google on Nov. 12 (Nov. 13 Japan time) released its AI model "Gemini 4 Hydrogen." While the higher-end "Gemini 4 Carbon" and "Gemini 4 Argon" take time to reason through hard problems, Google positions Hydrogen as a model that handles everyday tasks, coding and the work of AI agents that carry out tasks on their own quickly and efficiently. It is rolling out globally from the same day to developers, businesses and general users, including free users of the Gemini app and all users of Google Search.

Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet, announced it on X at 3:02:12 a.m. Nov. 13 Japan time. In the post, he said it finishes tasks 2.5 times faster than 3.8 Flash and offers a choice of four levels of thinking depth.

...

## API pricing is $1.50 input and $7.50 output

API pricing for developers calling the model from their own services is $1.50 for input and $7.50 for output per million tokens, the units of text the AI reads and writes. According to Google, the context window is 1 million tokens, and the same rate applies at any length within that range. The output price includes tokens for the thinking process before the model answers.

According to the Gemini API pricing page, the current Gemini 3.8 Flash costs $0.75 for input and $3.75 for output through Dec. 31, rising to $1.50 for input and $7.50 for output from Jan. 1, 2027. Hydrogen is priced the same as 3.8 Flash after that increase. The higher-end Gemini 4 Argon costs $2 for input and $10 for output through Nov. 30, and $4 for input and $20 for output from Dec. 1.

Gemini API paid tier prices (dollars per million tokens), from Google's pricing page

- Gemini 3.8 Flash (through Dec. 31)
- Gemini 4 Hydrogen
- Gemini 4 Argon (through Nov. 30)

According to the pricing page, Hydrogen is also available on the Gemini API free tier. Argon is not available on the free tier. Discounts for repeatedly sent input (caching) are available only through the automatically applied method, at $0.075 per million tokens.

...

Developers can use it on all tiers of Google AI Studio and the Gemini API. In the development tool Android Studio it is available on the paid tier, and in Antigravity it is available to paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

Businesses can use it in "Gemini for business" through the API or the model selector, as well as in Antigravity and in Gemini in Google Sheets for eligible business subscriptions.

...

In the Gemini 4 line, Google announced Argon on Oct. 1 (Japan time) and Carbon on Oct. 29, and began general availability of Carbon on Nov. 11 (article on Carbon's general availability). Hydrogen was officially announced about two and a half weeks after the post about its codename.
